rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline is competitive and how much later multiprofile, aggregation, or fusion complexity can add. config_001 tests the simplest RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline. It is the best first experiment because it establishes a low-complexity reference for the PCA_n2000 branch, avoids confounding with image, multiprofile, aggregation, or fusion choices, and creates a clear anchor for later comparisons.

Only RNA-only PCA singleprofile has been tested so far, with moderate performance (accuracy 0.485, F1 0.464), leaving major uncertainty about whether image features provide useful predictive signal. config_010 tests image-only singleprofile with ResNet50, matching the profile setting of the RNA baseline, so it isolates the modality effect before adding fusion or multiprofile complexity. It is the best next use of budget because it establishes a needed image baseline and informs whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile substantially outperforms image-only ResNet50 singleprofile (accuracy 0.485 vs 0.208; F1 0.464 vs 0.172), so the strongest current evidence favors RNA. config_002 tests whether multiprofile aggregation improves that RNA baseline while keeping the same PCA encoder, isolating the effect of profile setting and simple aggregation. Under limited budget, this is the best next step because it exploits the most promising modality with a simple, informative extension before investing in more complex encoders, transformers, or multimodal fusion.

The strongest result so far is config_002, where multiprofile PCA RNA with avgpool reaches 0.591 accuracy and 0.573 F1, clearly above singleprofile PCA RNA. However, the gain over config_001 could involve both multiprofile representation and aggregation, and the effect of aggregation is not yet isolated. config_003 tests transformer aggregation while keeping model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed, directly comparing it to avgpool under the current promising setup. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal one-factor extension of the best configuration, reduces uncertainty about whether a more complex aggregation is useful, and avoids spending budget on multiple simultaneous changes such as new encoders or multimodal fusion.

RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the strongest result so far, while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether the PCA representation is limiting in this best profile/aggregation setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile avgpool, isolating the representation effect. This exploits the promising RNA direction, likely maintains high validation accuracy, and provides a stronger RNA baseline before adding image/fusion complexity, making it an efficient next experiment.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile avgpool with scvi_n200 is best (accuracy 0.650, F1 0.628), and multiprofile avgpool also improved PCA over singleprofile. The key uncertainty is whether the scvi improvement is due to the learned encoder itself or to multiprofile averaging. config_004 tests scvi_n200 in the simpler singleprofile setting, isolating the profile-setting effect for the best RNA encoder. This is a single-factor extension of the most promising direction, has high expected utility, and clarifies whether a simpler RNA-only model may be sufficient before adding image modalities or more complex aggregation.

RNA-only multiprofile with scvi and avgpool is currently the strongest setting (config_005, acc 0.650), while pca multiprofile showed avgpool outperforming transformer (config_002 vs config_003). The main uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool for the stronger scvi representation. config_006 changes only aggregation relative to config_005, so it isolates this design choice while exploiting the most promising RNA direction, making it a more controlled and informative next step than testing scgpt or multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi is currently the strongest direction, with config_006 and config_005 nearly tied and avgpool at least as reliable as transformer. Image-only resnet50 is weak, so adding multimodal complexity now would confound several changes. config_008 tests only the RNA encoder by replacing scvi with scgpt under the same multiprofile/avgpool setting, clarifying whether representation choice can further improve the best-performing branch before moving to fusion.

RNA-only scvi multiprofile models are currently strongest (~0.65 accuracy/F1), while the only image-only result (resnet50 singleprofile) is very weak (~0.21 accuracy), leaving the value of the image modality uncertain. config_013 tests whether a stronger pretrained image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can make image features useful in the simplest singleprofile image-only setting, directly comparable to config_010 and isolating the image representation choice. This is a low-confound, high-information experiment: if ViT is weak, multimodal ViT configurations can be deprioritized; if ViT is strong, it justifies adding image features to the best RNA-only setup next.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile is much better than PCA or scGPT, and avgpool/transformer are nearly tied, with avgpool being simpler and robust. Image-only models are weak, so it is unclear whether image data can add value. This experiment tests whether adding a ViT image branch to the strong scvi multiprofile RNA model improves validation accuracy/F1 over the RNA-only baseline using a simple concat fusion. It is the best next step because it exploits the best RNA evidence while beginning multimodal exploration with the simplest informative fusion setting, reducing uncertainty about whether image information is useful before testing more complex fusion or aggregation choices.
